title: 'Gender apartheid': How the Taliban have trampled women's rights for five years
subhead: 'Voices of Afghan Women' (2/6). Here is the next installment of testimonies collected by our reporter in Kabul.

title: Why are heatwaves becoming more frequent in France?
subhead: Between May and July, France was the most abnormally hot country in the world, compared to its average heat index. While the role of global warming is not under debate, the frequency of this summer's heatwaves is a topic of scientific debate.

'We were petrified': Afghan women on the tragic day the Taliban came back
subhead: 'Voices of Afghan Women' (1/6). Five years after the Taliban returned to power and imposed their archaic version of Sharia law, our special correspondent in Kabul spoke with these almost invisible women about their daily fears, the oppressive grip of family, forced marriages and their stolen dreams.

title: Mahmoud Darwish and Tamar Ben Ami: The impossible love of a Palestinian poet and an Israeli dancer
subhead: In the early 1960s, in Haifa, Israel, the young Palestinian poet Mahmoud Darwish fell in love with Tamar Ben Ami, a Jewish Israeli dancer. Their romance was intense but brief. From this forbidden love, the writer composed a poignant poem, 'Rita and the Rifle,' which is still sung throughout the Arab world.

title: French court shuts down establishment hosting paid gang bangs in Paris
subhead: France's highest administrative court upheld the temporary closure of a venue that hosted these sexual activities in mid-July while awaiting a final ruling. The court found that the events at the establishment exposed women to 'serious risks' to their physical and psychological well-being, but it did not ban the practices themselves.
